The correction writes unresolved-send durability through module-level helpers that independently reload/write SERVICE_STATE_FILE (`persist_unresolved_send`, `attach_send_result`, `clear_unresolved_send`). The active DryRunLiveCopyService object does not merge those writes into `self.state`. In the real WS path, `process_ws_fill()` calls `self.process_fill(...)` and then `self.persist()`. In `run_once()`, the service also calls `self.persist()` after processing fills. `persist()` rewrites SERVICE_STATE_FILE from the older in-memory `self.state`.

Therefore a real send can durably write `in_flight_unresolved`, remain unresolved/partial/unknown, and then have that reservation erased moments later by the service's normal persist. On restart, no unresolved reservation may remain to block a duplicate/overlapping order. This violates the Architect's IN_FLIGHT_RECOVERY_RULE and SETTLEMENT_LIFECYCLE_RULE.

This is not an evidence-only issue and is not authorised to patch under the 422 candidate lock. Preserve 3113c59 byte-identical. No trim, no production edit, no G4.
